scope: ELR-SEC-105 only: fail-closed client access to analyticsEvents, removal of Flutter Firestore persistence and parameter logging, compatibility of existing invite/claim/share call sites, and correction of current privacy disclosures.
scopeLimit: This is not an application-wide privacy, analytics, Firebase, or Android release score. Historical analytics retention and deletion, trusted aggregate ingestion, quotas, deduplication, data dictionary approval, and pilot reporting remain blocked under ELR-OPS-405.
summary: The candidate tree denies every client read and write to analyticsEvents, and Android no longer persists telemetry or logs analytics parameters. Existing domain call sites remain non-blocking no-op boundaries. No Firebase, Hosting, Remote Config, or Android release deployment was performed.

evidence: firestore.rules uses allow read, write: if false for analyticsEvents
emulator attacks deny anonymous and authenticated get and list
historical documents seeded through the Admin test context remain inaccessible to clients
emulator attacks deny create, update, and delete even for formerly accepted schemas
forgeable analytics schema validators were removed from Firestore rules
Admin SDK account-deletion access remains outside client rules
AnalyticsService has no Cloud Firestore, FirebasePaths, UUID, or developer.log dependency
invite, claim, join, Pride, export, and share callbacks retain their public signatures without persistence
AnalyticsService is an explicit no-op compatibility boundary with no observer or alternate production sink
the in-app and Hosting privacy text disclose the temporary analytics pause and possible historical records
the data inventory records blocked client access and the open retention gap
ADR-002 no longer claims a persisted analytics event

sourceGuard.contract: clientAnalyticsAccess rejects FirebasePaths.analyticsEvents and raw analyticsEvents collection access from every Flutter file

remainingRisks.risk: Historical documents may retain nested stable identifiers and have no approved TTL or purge process; trusted aggregate measurement is not implemented.
Trusted audit, voting, and atomic dispute operations remain the next backend critical path.
Private and public player data are not yet separated by the final projection model.

recommendations: Keep analyticsEvents denied until ELR-OPS-405 passes its own privacy, abuse, deletion, and reporting gate.
Do not turn the no-op compatibility boundary into a client measurement backend.
Review and approve historical retention and deletion before the staged market pilot.
Review these prototype rules before any production deployment.
releaseDecision: ELR-SEC-105 containment passes locally. Android V1 release remains blocked by Waves 1 through 5 and no deployment is authorized by this audit.
